title: Colonoscopy Preparation
summary:
A clean colon saves lives. Preparing for your upcoming colonoscopy might feel overwhelming, but a successful bowel prep allows your VA GI Team to clearly see the lining of your colon, detect hidden polyps, and prevent colorectal cancer. If the colon isn’t completely clean, your procedure may have to be rescheduled. 

This step-by-step video guide walks you through what to do, what to eat, what medication to stop, and how to take your prescribed VA bowel prep solution so you can show up for your appointment with confidence. 

Please follow the specific instruction letter mailed to you or provided by your local VA GI clinic, as individual instructions may vary based on your medical history and the specific prep kit prescribed to you. If you have questions about your medications—especially blood thinners or diabetes management—contact your local VA GI clinic.

Thank you for your service and thank you for choosing the VA for your health care services.

Credits:
This educational video was developed and produced by the clinical team at the Dallas VA Medical Center Gastroenterology (GI) Lab.
• Clinical Contributors: Dallas VA GI Nurses (S. Ruiz, G. K. Escuin, S. Inductivo, K. Hernandez)

In this conversation, Chief McDonnell explains how staffing and recruitment affect emergency response and community policing, what police leaders can do to support morale, and how Los Angeles is preparing for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games. They also discuss regional and federal partnerships, drone and cyber threats, international coordination, and why public safety is a team sport.

Recorded September 2, 2026. Staffing figures and plans reflect the discussion at that time.

title: How Flock Cameras Cut Beverly Hills Crime 34%
summary:
Retired Beverly Hills Police Chief Mark Stainbrook sits down with Your LEO Nation and walks through the system he built after his first night on the job — the night Jacqueline Avant was murdered.

He covers the constitutional fight over Flock cameras and ALPRs, why public streets are not a privacy zone, and how BHPD combined license-plate readers at every entrance, live cameras, and drones into a military-style command center. Stolen-car recoveries jumped from about 50 a year to more than 200. Arrests rose 22%. Career criminals got a “jail card” warning them: come here to steal, and this technology will find you.

Stainbrook also tells the story of a suspect tied to four murders in four days whose plate hit coming into the city — officers were on the car in two minutes, recovered the gun, and ballistics linked the killings. He breaks down audits, two-year video retention, supervisor oversight, fewer bad stops, lower liability, and why 600-plus agencies came to study the model.
